name: Solon
why: Athenian lawgiver associated with debt relief and political reform.

name: Cleisthenes
why: Reorganized Athenian political structures and helped deepen democracy.

name: Herodotus
why: Historian known for inquiry, travel, evidence, and explanations of the Persian Wars.

name: Socrates
why: Used questioning to examine virtue, justice, and knowledge.

name: Plato
why: Developed theories of Forms, philosophical education, and ideal government.

name: Aristotle
why: Favored observation, classification, and practical analysis of real constitutions.

name: Hippocrates
why: Associated with naturalistic medicine, observation, and medical ethics.

name: Aristarchus
why: Proposed an early heliocentric model.

name: Cyrus the Great
why: Founded the Achaemenid Persian Empire by defeating Median rule and expanding Persian power.

name: Darius I
why: Expanded and administered the Persian Empire while facing revolts and Greek resistance.

name: Xerxes I
why: Led the major Persian invasion of Greece in 480 BCE.

name: Pericles
why: Athenian statesman associated with democracy, empire, building, and the early Peloponnesian War.

name: Thrasybulus
why: Helped overthrow the Thirty Tyrants and restore Athenian democracy.

name: Philip II
why: Strengthened Macedonia and brought much of Greece under Macedonian leadership.

name: Alexander the Great
why: Conquered the Persian Empire and accelerated Hellenistic cultural diffusion.

name: Cincinnatus
why: Roman model of civic virtue and temporary emergency power.

name: Hannibal
why: Carthaginian commander who invaded Italy during the Second Punic War.

name: Scipio Africanus
why: Roman commander who defeated Hannibal at Zama.

name: Julius Caesar
why: General and dictator whose civil war accelerated the Republic’s collapse.

name: Augustus
why: First Roman emperor in practice; established the principate while preserving republican forms.

name: Agrippina the Elder
why: Example of an elite Roman woman exercising significant informal political and military influence.
